1- Aflac.pdf.name: Aflac
1- Aflac.pdf.balance_sheet_text: Balance Sheet Strength: Strongest • • • • • Historically, risk-adjusted capitalization has consistently been maintained at the strongest categorization, as measured by Best's Capital Adequacy Ratio (BCAR) model. Shareholders' equity increased in the second quarter of 2025 following improvement in unrealized foreign currency translation loss over the previous year-ended. The group's product reserves are more than adequate and remain sufficient under numerous scenarios. The organization's invested assets are diverse across asset classes and types, and they are managed both internally and through highly respected external asset managers. The portfolio has undergone continued de-risking and trade activity. However, the group has continued to report an increase in commercial mortgage transition real estate delinquencies and resulting increase in group real estate owned. Moreover, AM Best acknowledges that the mortgage and real estate portfolio consists of a small but material portion of Aflac’s invested assets. In addition to the external reinsurance, the organization is increasing its use of internal reinsurance through the use of Aflac Re Bermuda Ltd. (Aflac Re), a Bermuda reinsurer. Aflac Re is utilized to reinsure a portion of long-term liabilities from Aflac Life Insurance Japan (Aflac Japan). Foreign exchange risk has been a challenge but has been mitigated through hedging programs and more recently benefited from a weakening of the Japanese yen.

10 - Atlantic American Bankers Fidelity..name: Atlantic American — Bankers Fidelity
10 - Atlantic American Bankers Fidelity..balance_sheet_text: Balance Sheet Strength: Very Strong • • • • Bankers Fidelity Life Insurance Group (BFLIG) maintains a very strong level of risk-adjusted capitalization for its insurance, investment and business risks as measured by Best's Capital Adequacy Ratio (BCAR). The BCAR declined to the very strong level in 2024 from the strongest level in the prior year. Capital and surplus has fluctuated over the last five years, reflecting a negative 3.4% five-year compound annual growth rate at year-end 2025, mainly due to unrealized capital losses and dividends paid to its parent company exceeding capital contributions received from its parent company. Benefits from contingent liquidity and financial flexibility via an undrawn line of credit with the Federal Home Loan Bank of Atlanta. While the majority of invested assets consist of investment-grade fixed-income securities, 47.7% of these are higher-risk NAIC Class 2 issues, which materially exceeds the average for life and health carriers. Also, equity holdings, while relatively small, are concentrated in one entity.

11 - CNO Bankers Life.pdf.name: CNO — Bankers Life
11 - CNO Bankers Life.pdf.balance_sheet_text: Balance Sheet Strength: Very Strong • • • • Risk-adjusted capitalization is assessed as strong as measured by Best’s Capital Adequacy Ratio (BCAR). Both the parent and the operating entities have strong liquidity measures with adequate holding company cash on hand. The parent company has access to capital from the Federal Home Loan Bank. Assets and liabilities are well matched across all asset classes. Uses reinsurance strategically to move risk off its balance sheet and has moved business into an affiliated Bermuda captive.

12 - CNO Colonial Penn.pdf.name: CNO — Colonial Penn
12 - CNO Colonial Penn.pdf.balance_sheet_text: Balance Sheet Strength: Very Strong • • • • Risk-adjusted capitalization is assessed as strong as measured by Best’s Capital Adequacy Ratio (BCAR). Both the parent and the operating entities have strong liquidity measures with adequate holding company cash on hand. The parent company has access to capital from the Federal Home Loan Bank. Assets and liabilities are well matched across all asset classes. Uses reinsurance strategically to move risk off its balance sheet and has moved business into an affiliated Bermuda captive.

13 - Combined Insurance (Chubb).pdf.name: Combined Insurance (Chubb)
13 - Combined Insurance (Chubb).pdf.balance_sheet_text: Balance Sheet Strength: Strong • • • Combined A&H Group's balance sheet strength assessment of strong is based on the strong level of risk-adjusted capitalization at year-end 2024 and at the third quarter of 2025 as measured by Best's Capital Adequacy Ratio (BCAR) at the 99.6% VaR confidence level, as well as other mildly positive quantitative and qualitative considerations. The group has a strong liquidity position with short and long ratios at 999% and 466.4%, respectively. The investment portfolio is viewed as high quality, with a nominal allocation to below-investment-grade bonds.

14 - Continental General.pdf.name: Continental General
14 - Continental General.pdf.balance_sheet_text: Balance Sheet Strength: Strong • • • • The risk-adjusted capitalization of Continental General Insurance Company (CGIC) remains at the very strong level as measured by Best's Capital Adequacy Ratio (BCAR). The company has successfully grown its absolute level of capital, net premiums, and invested assets through primarily a series of acquisitions of closed blocks of long-term care (LTC) insurance business. The investment portfolio mainly includes fixed-income securities with good credit quality, as well as an allocation in value-oriented equities that can help achieve real returns to match longer-duration inflation-linked liabilities. Significant volatility in unrealized capital gains or losses in its equity investment portfolio is stabilized by increases or decreases in the asset valuation reserve, respectively; however, these equity investments represent a material percentage of CGIC's capital and surplus.

15 - Aetna, Cvs - Continental LIfe.pdf.name: Aetna/CVS — Continental Life
15 - Aetna, Cvs - Continental LIfe.pdf.balance_sheet_text: Balance Sheet Strength: Very Strong • • • • The group maintains the strongest level of risk-adjusted capitalization, as measured by Best's Capital Adequacy Ratio (BCAR) as of year-end 2024, and it is expected to remain at this level through 2025. While the BCAR at the 99.6% VaR declined in 2024, it is projected to improve in 2025 due to an improvement in net earnings. The group's investment portfolio is managed at the enterprise level and has maintained a conservative risk appetite over the past few years, being mainly concentrated in investment-grade fixed-income securities and cash and cash equivalents. The group's strategy gives priority to liquidity. Liquidity measures are at an adequate level and are expected to improve as earnings improve. The group's financial flexibility is significantly strengthened by access to a large credit facility at the Federal Home Loan Bank of Boston. Aetna Health & Life Group maintains a quota share reinsurance agreement with Health Re, Inc., and subsequent excess of loss protection by Vitality Re Limited entities, which allow the group to reduce its required capital and provide $900 million of collateralized coverage on its group commercial business in case of an unexpected rise in the medical benefit ratio.

17 - Forethought - Global Atlantic.pdf.name: Forethought (Global Atlantic)
17 - Forethought - Global Atlantic.pdf.balance_sheet_text: Balance Sheet Strength: Very Strong • • • • Risk-adjusted capitalization continues to be assessed as strong as measured by Best's Capital Adequacy Ratio (BCAR) in support of its insurance, investment, and operational risks. The organization has demonstrated a sustained trend of strong-assessed capitalization. Growth in financial flexibility has been supported by consistently strong earnings, access to debt in the financial markets, and contributions from the holding companies. The group's parent company, KKR & Company Inc. (NYSE: KKR), is anticipated to continue to bolster balance sheet support as it has demonstrated over the last few years. The investment portfolio maintains an elevated allocation to structured securities and other non-traditional fixed-income assets relative to industry averages and is supported by appropriate capital levels required to manage the risk associated with these types of assets. The organization has demonstrated financial flexibility and asset/liability management (ALM), supporting the capital position and overall balance sheet.

18 - FDLIC.pdf.name: Funeral Directors Life
18 - FDLIC.pdf.balance_sheet_text: Balance Sheet Strength: Very Strong • • • • The risk-adjusted capitalization of Funeral Directors Group (Funeral Directors) has been assessed within the very strong category as measured by Best’s Capital Adequacy Ratio (BCAR). Capital has consistently increased year over year with a 6.6% five-year CAGR. The capital growth is driven by retained earnings. The investment portfolio is managed by an affiliate, Parkway Advisors LP, and has had consistently higher yields than industry averages. However, the group has a relatively high allocation to class 2 bonds and below-investment-grade bonds. The group has maintained sufficient liquidity and consistent operating cash flows in both high and low interest rate environments.

19 - GPM.pdf.name: Government Personnel Mutual
19 - GPM.pdf.balance_sheet_text: Balance Sheet Strength: Very Strong • • • • GPM Life Group maintains the strongest level of risk-adjusted capitalization as measured by Best's Capital Adequacy Ratio (BCAR). Risk profile of the group's investment portfolio is viewed as in line with peers, as the group's bond holdings are of strong credit quality and mortgage holdings are in good standing. Capital and surplus increase primarily caused by benefit and expense management. Appropriate use of reinsurance to alleviate some of the new sales strain and protect capital and surplus.

2 - American Amicable, Trinity.pdf.name: American-Amicable / Trinity
2 - American Amicable, Trinity.pdf.balance_sheet_text: Balance Sheet Strength: Very Strong • • • IA American Life Group (IAALG) has maintained the strongest level of risk-adjusted capitalization as measured by Best's Capital Adequacy Ratio (BCAR) over the long term through both retained earnings and capital contributions from the parent company. Material use of reinsurance relative to peers historically, however, this has declined over time and ceded business is to primarily high-rated counterparties. The group manages a conservative investment portfolio that is heavily weighted in investment-grade fixed-income securities with only minor holdings in mortgage loans, real estate, and Schedule BA assets.

20 - GTL.pdf.name: Guarantee Trust Life
20 - GTL.pdf.balance_sheet_text: Balance Sheet Strength: Strongest • • • • The risk-adjusted capitalization of Guarantee Trust Life Insurance Company (GTL) is assessed at the strongest level based on its Best's Capital Adequacy Ratio (BCAR) for its insurance and investment risks. Adequate liquidity ratios and positive operating cash flows. Maintains an average-risk investment portfolio managed by several asset management firms focused on their respective investment specialties. Enhanced financial flexibility via its membership since 2022 in the Federal Home Loan Bank of Chicago with access to funds for spread-based investing and liquidity (if needed).

21 - globe life.pdf.name: Globe Life
21 - globe life.pdf.balance_sheet_text: Balance Sheet Strength: Strong • • • • The risk-adjusted capitalization of Globe Life Group (Globe Life) has been assessed within the strong category, as measured by Best’s Capital Adequacy Ratio (BCAR), and year-end capital and surplus increased year over year. Liquidity profile is enhanced by strong cash flows, Federal Home Loan Bank (FHLB) lending, and a robust commercial paper program backed by a high-quality bank line of credit. Reinsurance reliance is minimal as Globe Life issues low-face amount policies. Reinsurance utilizes high-quality carriers. Long track record of increasing invested assets and stable allocation. The investment portfolio is managed on a consolidated basis and is primarily allocated to investment-grade bonds (evenly split between Class 1 & 2) with an increasing allocation to Schedule BA assets. Also, the group’s high-risk assets to capital and surplus ratio is comparatively higher than its peers.

22 - Guardian LIfe.pdf.name: Guardian Life
22 - Guardian LIfe.pdf.balance_sheet_text: Balance Sheet Strength: Strongest • • • • • • Guardian Life Group (Guardian) maintains the strongest level of risk-adjusted capitalization as measured by Best's Capital Adequacy Ratio (BCAR), and the group has taken steps to reduce its balance sheet risks, for example, by reinsuring its in-force variable annuity block and gradually enhancing the sale of fee-based lower-risk and capital-light products such as dental and vision insurance. A majority of the general account liabilities are interest sensitive; however, Guardian’s liabilities overall are supported by well- matched assets, and the group maintains a relatively conservative and diverse investment portfolio for its retained assets. This is demonstrated by its overall surplus remaining robust in a continued higher or lower interest rate environment under its New York 7 cash flow stress testing. Guardian also utilizes external reinsurance with well-rated counterparties for a range of fixed deferred annuity product sales to prudently manage capital. Due to the higher interest rate environment primarily, its fixed-income portfolio is in an unrealized capital loss position; however, management expects these assets to be held-to-maturity and matched against liability and liquidity needs, and the group closely monitors its credit risks through watch lists and regular impairment testing. Guardian has strong liquidity measures driven by good cash flows from its regulated and non-regulated subsidiaries, and it has access to contingent liquidity, if necessary. The organization maintains favorable financial and operating leverage in the form of surplus notes and funding agreements, respectively, and interest coverage ratios that are within AM Best's tolerances for the current rating levels.

23 - Cigna National Health.pdf.name: Cigna — National Health
23 - Cigna National Health.pdf.balance_sheet_text: Balance Sheet Strength: Very Strong • • • • The HCSC Medicare & Supplemental Group has a Best's Capital Adequacy Ratio (BCAR) in the strongest category that AM Best expects will be bolstered and supported to maintain the group's balance sheet metrics at favorable levels. In addition, capital and surplus growth has historically been supported by fluctuating underwriting results and investment income across most of the entities in the group. These entities maintain a prudent and diversified investment portfolio with good credit quality. Nearly all invested assets are held in investment-grade fixed-income securities. AM Best notes that the organization also holds sizable receivables from the federal government related to its Medicare business. Net cash flow from operations remains favorable. Liquidity measures remain adequate and are strengthened by access at the lead entity, Health Care Service Corporation (HCSC).

24 - Heartland National.pdf.name: Heartland National
24 - Heartland National.pdf.balance_sheet_text: Balance Sheet Strength: Strong • • • • The risk-adjusted capitalization of Heartland National Life (HNL) was assessed at the level of strong at year-end 2024, as measured by Best’s Capital Adequacy Ratio (BCAR); however, HNL's overall balance sheet strength assessment is pressured by rapid annuity growth that has been heavily reinsured, which has increased reinsurance counterparty risk and operational risk. The company has a chief risk officer (CRO) in place; however, HNL refiled its year-end 2024 statutory statement following an external audit of its net deferred tax asset, which depends on the company's future expected profits and which detracts from the company's quality of assets and capital. A high percent of available capital also related to agent balances in the course of collection. Partially offsetting these negative credit rating factors is HNL's execution of its capital plans, which have included annuity reinsurance with Converge Re II (Puerto Rico), a surplus note funded by HNL's parent company, and a possible new equity partner along with additional diversified reinsurance options. HNL has access to capital through both its principal owner and a strategic partner, which have infused capital contributions to support HNL's liabilities and business growth to some extent.

25 - Homesteaders LIfe.pdf.name: Homesteaders Life
25 - Homesteaders LIfe.pdf.balance_sheet_text: Balance Sheet Strength: Strong • • • • • Risk-adjusted capitalization is assessed as strong as measured by Best’s Capital Adequacy Ratio (BCAR). Homesteaders’ BCAR has shown a steady decline over recent periods due primarily to its strategic investments in non-admitted statutory assets. Year-end 2025 capital and surplus (C&S) increased from the prior year-end due to gains from operations. Financial leverage was eliminated from the balance sheet in 2025 due to the conversion of two surplus notes to common equity. Homesteaders maintains a high-quality, liquid investment portfolio expertly managed by external asset managers. Allocation to commercial mortgages has increased in recent periods due primarily to the company's funeral home lending program. Homesteaders has two additional sources of liquidity through a bank line of credit and borrowing capacity via its Federal Home Loan Bank (FHLB) membership.

26 - HUmana.pdf.name: Humana
26 - HUmana.pdf.balance_sheet_text: Balance Sheet Strength: Adequate • • • • The aggregate risk-adjusted capitalization of Humana’s lead health and life companies is maintained at a weak level, as measured by Best's Capital Adequacy Ratio (BCAR). Over the last five years, strong premium growth has outpaced capital and surplus growth due to subsidiary dividends to the parent entity. The weak BCAR assessment is partially offset by solid liquidity measures and a prudent invested asset portfolio, resulting in an adequate balance sheet strength assessment. While premium has grown at an 11.2% compound annual growth rate (CAGR), capital and surplus has grown at a 9.8% CAGR over the last five years through robust earnings and capital contributions from the parent and is partially offset by subsidiary dividends to the parent organization. Capital modeling and stress testing are performed annually. Capital management is conducted at the enterprise level, as well as at individual insurance entities with targeted regulatory capital thresholds. The parent entity has sufficient liquidity to provide capital contributions to entities when necessary through its cash holdings, commercial paper program, access to debt markets, and non-regulated cash flows from Humana Inc.'s CenterWell segment. The group maintains a conservative investment allocation that is predominantly composed of investment-grade fixed-income securities and cash and short-term investments.

27 - Investors Heritage.pdf.name: Investors Heritage
27 - Investors Heritage.pdf.balance_sheet_text: Balance Sheet Strength: Adequate • • • • Investors Heritage Life's Best's Capital Adequacy Ratio (BCAR) assessment improved from weak to strong in 2024. The company has experienced volatility in the BCAR scores in recent years as it manages new business strain from strong annuity sales. Growth in capital has historically been supported by capital contributions from the parent to offset the new business strain from strong annuity sales. Reinsurance leverage, which is below the industry average, has increased in recent years. The investment portfolio's risk profile is in line with peers and has good diversification across investment asset classes.

28 - Liberty Bankers.pdf.name: Liberty Bankers
28 - Liberty Bankers.pdf.balance_sheet_text: Balance Sheet Strength: Very Strong • • • • The risk-adjusted capitalization of Liberty Bankers Insurance Group (Liberty Bankers) has now been assessed within the strongest category, as measured by Best's Capital Adequacy Ratio (BCAR). Moderately risky investment profile with a high allocation to NAIC Class 2 bonds and a significant portion of assets with real estate exposure. The real estate exposure risk is partially mitigated by the group’s in-house expertise in this asset class. The group's exposure to Schedule BA assets has seen an overall reduction the last few years. Reserves are adequate to meet contractual obligations at all group levels, as per internal cash flow testing analysis. The group has increased its reinsurance usage in 2024, but it is still below peers and the industry average.

29 - Lincoln Financial.pdf.name: Lincoln Financial
29 - Lincoln Financial.pdf.balance_sheet_text: Balance Sheet Strength: Strong • • • • • Risk-adjusted capitalization is categorized as very strong as measured by Best's Capital Adequacy Ratio (BCAR); however, the quality of capital is somewhat diminished by high utilization of captive, other affiliate, and external reinsurance for life insurance and annuity reserves with generally well-rated counterparties. A high proportion of general account liabilities are interest sensitive; however, the overall asset-liability duration metrics of Lincoln Financial Insurance Group (Lincoln) are well matched, and the group has taken various steps to reduce its balance sheet risks including reinsurance, optimized hedging, and managing the volume and mix of sales by product. Due to the higher interest rate environment primarily, Lincoln's fixed-income portfolio is in an unrealized capital loss position; however, management expects these assets to be held-to-maturity and matched against liability and liquidity needs, and the group closely monitors its credit risks through watchlists and regular impairment testing. Financial leverage ratio has remained close to Lincoln's 25% target; however, the group has a track record of maintaining good financial flexibility through access to additional liquidity sources, including the debt capital markets, contingent capital, bank credit, Federal Home Loan Bank membership, internal surplus notes and, more recently, funding agreement-backed notes that contribute to some operating leverage. Diversified liability profile includes life insurance, annuity, group protection, and retirement plan services lines of business sold in both retail and institutional markets.

3 - Aetna, Cvs - American Continental.pd.balance_sheet_text: Balance Sheet Strength: Very Strong • • • • The group maintains the strongest level of risk-adjusted capitalization, as measured by Best's Capital Adequacy Ratio (BCAR) as of year-end 2024, and it is expected to remain at this level through 2025. 30 - Cigna Loyal American.pdf.name: Cigna — Loyal American
30 - Cigna Loyal American.pdf.balance_sheet_text: Balance Sheet Strength: Very Strong • • • • The HCSC Medicare & Supplemental Group has a Best's Capital Adequacy Ratio (BCAR) in the strongest category that AM Best expects will be bolstered and supported to maintain the group's balance sheet metrics at favorable levels. In addition, capital and surplus growth has historically been supported by fluctuating underwriting results and investment income across most of the entities in the group. These entities maintain a prudent and diversified investment portfolio with good credit quality. Nearly all invested assets are held in investment-grade fixed-income securities. Liquidity measures remain adequate and are strengthened by access at the lead entity, Health Care Service Corporation (HCSC).

32 - Manhattan LIfe Group.pdf.name: ManhattanLife — Assurance
32 - Manhattan LIfe Group.pdf.balance_sheet_text: Balance Sheet Strength: Adequate • • • • Manhattan Insurance Group has shown a trend of improving risk-adjusted capitalization over the previous several years with results, as measured by Best's Capital Adequacy Ratio (BCAR), indicating a continued very strong assessment for year-end 2024. The group has historically managed its capital well while acquiring blocks of business. However, the group has pivoted to more organic growth with the sale of its two charters, which helps elevate its overall capital. The group has started to allocate more to NAIC-1 bonds and mortgage loans the past two years and has maintained liquidity ratios with increased holdings in cash and short-term investments. The group has continued to focus on reducing its level of financial leverage, but it still maintains accumulated goodwill from acquisition activity and surplus notes.

33 - Mutual of Omaha.pdf.name: Mutual of Omaha
33 - Mutual of Omaha.pdf.balance_sheet_text: Balance Sheet Strength: Very Strong • • • • • Mutual of Omaha Group maintains the strongest level of risk-adjusted capitalization as measured by Best's Capital Adequacy Ratio (BCAR) at the 99.6% VaR. Mutual of Omaha Group has generated favorable capital and surplus growth over the past four years and through 2025 as a result of accumulation of net income in select years. Mutual of Omaha Group consistently reports positive liquidity metrics and has additional flexibility to support potential liquidity needs with borrowing capacity from the Federal Home Loan Bank. While Mutual of Omaha Group’s operating leverage is primarily due to its funding agreement-backed note program, the overall metrics remain within AM Best’s guidelines. Furthermore, the group’s financial leverage remains adequate. The group maintains a highly diversified investment portfolio with good credit quality. In addition, the group benefits from a solid liquidity position supported by liquid investment holdings.

34 - NGL.pdf.name: National Guardian Life
34 - NGL.pdf.balance_sheet_text: Balance Sheet Strength: Very Strong • • • NGL Insurance Group (NGL) has maintained the strongest level of risk-adjusted capitalization as measured by Best's Capital Adequacy Ratio (BCAR) over the long term, further bolstered by a favorable liquidity position. While the group has extended investment into Schedule BA categorized funds over the previous several years, the overall investment portfolio remains conservative and is heavily weighted in investment-grade bonds. Capital and surplus has been supported by several surplus notes that slightly decrease the quality of capital overall; however, financial leverage ratios have improved over the previous several years as the group continues to pay these notes down over time.

35 - Naitonal Western LIfe.pdf.name: National Western Life
35 - Naitonal Western LIfe.pdf.balance_sheet_text: Balance Sheet Strength: Very Strong • • • • The company maintains the strongest level of risk-adjusted capitalization as measured by Best's Capital Adequacy Ratio (BCAR). Balance sheet strength is expected to be impacted by planned capital withdrawals as part of the acquisition by Prosperity Life Group. The investment portfolio is conservative and has a low percentage of high-risk assets offset in part by significant holdings of NAIC Class 2 bonds. Additional yield is added via strategic use of asset-backed securities and private placement. Product reserves are heavily concentrated in fixed indexed annuities. Risk was lessened with utilization of reinsurance agreements.

36 - New Era Life.pdf.name: New Era Life
36 - New Era Life.pdf.balance_sheet_text: Balance Sheet Strength: Strong • • • New Era’s risk-adjusted capitalization is assessed within the strongest category, as measured by Best’s Capital Adequacy Ratio (BCAR). New Era has increased the allocation of below-investment-grade bonds in recent years, except in 2024 when the allocation decreased. This strategy began in 2020 in order to enhance the yield of the invested asset portfolio, but it also introduces more risk to the balance sheet. New Era has limited financial flexibility but adequate liquidity and cash flows to support operations.

37 - New York Life.pdf.name: New York Life
37 - New York Life.pdf.balance_sheet_text: Balance Sheet Strength: Strongest • • • • New York Life Group's (NYL) risk-adjusted capitalization is at the strong level as measured by Best's Capital Adequacy Ratio (BCAR), with ample financial flexibility along with continued strong liquidity to meet demand for obligations under stress scenarios. These positive qualitative factors support a balance sheet assessment level of strongest given the group operates as a New York regulated insurance enterprise, holding full statutory reserves funded by policyholder premiums, has greater asset adequacy requirements than a non-New York company and does not employ any permitted practices. Rigorous annual liquidity stress testing is performed and designed to capture tail-risk events. Reserve profile is weighted towards annuity products; this reserve profile is partially driven by the reserving dynamics between life insurance and annuity products, which generate higher reserves for annuity products in the earlier years. When Net Amount at Risk (NAR) for life insurance is included with reserves, NYL is heavily weighted towards life insurance. NYL has maintained strong reserves, posting a record high surplus in the current year while providing record high dividends to its policyholders. A well-diversified investment portfolio with a consistent approach towards credit risk and cash flow with a long-term view has been a strength for the group.

38 - Pekin LIfe.pdf.name: Pekin Life
38 - Pekin LIfe.pdf.balance_sheet_text: Balance Sheet Strength: Very Strong • • • Pekin Life Insurance Company (Pekin Life) maintains the strongest level of risk-adjusted capitalization as measured by Best's Capital Adequacy Ratio (BCAR) at the 99.6% confidence level. Prior to 2023, organic capital growth was on a declining trend over the most recent five-year period. However, admitted assets have seen an increasing trend over the same time period. Capital grew modestly in 2024. Pekin Life has a highly diverse investment portfolio that is of good credit quality.

39 - Philadelphia American.pdf.name: Philadelphia American
39 - Philadelphia American.pdf.balance_sheet_text: Balance Sheet Strength: Strong • • • New Era’s risk-adjusted capitalization is assessed within the strongest category, as measured by Best’s Capital Adequacy Ratio (BCAR). New Era has increased the allocation of below-investment-grade bonds in recent years, except in 2024 when the allocation decreased. This strategy began in 2020 in order to enhance the yield of the invested asset portfolio, but it also introduces more risk to the balance sheet. New Era has limited financial flexibility but adequate liquidity and cash flows to support operations.

4 - American National.pdf.name: American National
4 - American National.pdf.balance_sheet_text: Balance Sheet Strength: Very Strong • • • Very strong level of risk-adjusted capitalization as measured by Best's Capital Adequacy Ratio (BCAR). Overall capital levels remain favorable. Invested assets are well managed and good credit quality. The portfolio does have some exposure to higher-risk assets. Favorable quality of surplus, supported by earnings growth; growing use of reinsurance and no financial leverage.

40 - Physicians Mutual.pdf.name: Physicians Mutual
40 - Physicians Mutual.pdf.balance_sheet_text: Balance Sheet Strength: Strongest • • • • Physicians Mutual Group's risk-adjusted capitalization as measured by Best's Capital Adequacy Ratio (BCAR) is maintained at the strongest level. Financial flexibility has been enhanced by access to over $200 million of borrowing capacity under the Federal Home Loan Bank of Topeka, Kansas. Operating leverage is considered low and within an acceptable range. Quality of capital supported by organic earnings and low operating leverage metrics. Additionally, the group has reported an increase in capital and surplus through mid-2025. The investment strategy is relatively conservative and has placed more focus on liquid asset classes and asset/liability management. In addition, it maintains a conservative investment portfolio compared to the industry, consisting primarily of investment-grade fixed-income securities.

41 - Kemper Reserve National.pdf.name: Kemper — Reserve National
41 - Kemper Reserve National.pdf.balance_sheet_text: Balance Sheet Strength: Very Strong • • • • Reserve National Insurance Company's (RNIC) risk-adjusted capitalization, as measured by Best's Capital Adequacy Ratio, is assessed at the strongest level. The company continues to comfortably exceed the risk-based capital requirements specified by the NAIC. In 2024, capital and surplus grew to $66.4 million. RNIC's overall liquidity is supported by strong cash flow generation, excess capital and a conservative investment portfolio. The support from its parent, Medical Mutual of Ohio (MMO), provides the company with additional financial flexibility. However, as part of the organization's broader capital management strategy and RNIC's strong earnings in recent years, management anticipates upstreaming dividends to the parent company when appropriate.

43 - Sentinel Security Life.pdf.name: Sentinel Security Life
43 - Sentinel Security Life.pdf.balance_sheet_text: Balance Sheet Strength: Adequate • • • • The balance sheet assessment of A-CAP Group (ACAP) is impacted by consideration of a pending capital raise on the financial condition of the group. A-CAP faces an elevated risk profile driven by its elevated levels of reinsurance leverage, weak regulatory capital position and presence of illiquid assets. The group has assets that are not traditionally associated with insurance company investments, such as European football clubs and aviation. There is a duration mismatch with its liabilities, a concentration in individual securities, investments in affiliated assets and concentration in thinly traded Level 3 assets where quoted market prices are not generally available and the Company then uses third party valuations and alternative processes to calculate Fair Market Value for these assets. The group has concentrated reinsurance leverage even after recapturing the treaty with 777 Re in the first quarter of 2024. It utilizes a mix of rated and unrated unaffiliated reinsuring counterparties, both at the rated entities and at captives, as well as an unrated operating company. The risk of the unrated counterparties is mitigated using collateralized reinsurance agreements. Current regulatory capital ratios have deteriorated since 2023.

44 - American National Standard Life and.name: American National — Standard Life & Accident
44 - American National Standard Life and.balance_sheet_text: Balance Sheet Strength: Very Strong • • Strongest level of risk-adjusted capitalization, as measured by Best's Capital Adequacy Ratio (BCAR) at the VaR 99.6% level. This position is supported by the company's low underwriting risk and conservative investment allocations consisting primarily of cash and short-term investments, with minor allocations to high-quality long-term bonds. Financial flexibility is available through the company's much larger parent organization, Core Specialty Insurance Holdings, Inc. (Core Specialty).

45 - USAA Life.pdf.name: USAA Life
45 - USAA Life.pdf.balance_sheet_text: Balance Sheet Strength: Very Strong • • • Strongest level of risk-adjusted capitalization as measured by Best's Capital Adequacy Ratio (BCAR) scores at the VaR 99.6% level. Favorable financial flexibility with established access to capital and liquidity through its affiliated financing company and the Federal Home Loan Bank. The investment portfolio is viewed as high credit quality with modest allocations to higher-risk asset classes.

46 - UHC.pdf.name: UnitedHealthcare
46 - UHC.pdf.balance_sheet_text: Balance Sheet Strength: Strong • • • • Very strong Best's Capital Adequacy Ratio (BCAR) of 13.7 at the 99.6% VaR. Capital growth supported by consistently favorable earnings from operations offset by large dividends to the parent. Risk-adjusted capital has remained stable. Solid consolidated statutory risk-based capital. Ratio has remained in the targeted range of 225-250% company action level. Conservative investment portfolio that is held predominantly in investment-grade fixed-income securities and cash & short-term investments. Nominal exposure to equities and mortgage loans. Low level of invested asset risk. Strong liquidity supported by favorable operating cash flows, short-duration investment portfolio and high level of cash. 9 - Assurity.pdf.balance_sheet_text: Balance Sheet Strength: Strongest • • • • The risk-adjusted capitalization of Assurity Life Insurance Group (Assurity Life Group), as measured by Best's Capital Adequacy Ratio (BCAR), is assessed as being at the strongest level and supports the group’s business, investment and insurance risks. Additionally, the balance sheet maintains ample liquidity and a capital base driven by retained earnings. The group’s invested asset portfolio is primarily of good credit quality, holding highly rated investment-grade bonds while attempting to enhance total yield through commercial mortgage loan holdings, private placements, securities lending, and Federal Home Loan Bank borrowing. While mortgage holdings are elevated relative to the life industry average, this portfolio has performed with very few troubled loans over the past decade, supported by good loan-to-value ratios and debt service coverage ratios. Moderate but prudent use of reinsurance, with a reinsurance leverage ratio well below the life industry average.
